geometry.polygon: Wide-base inverted V (A-frame): two long leg lines from a broad foot base to the hip hinge, then a lengthened spine vector toward the floor; optional crown contact as a soft third point.
geometry.summary: Feet stand wide and parallel (or toes slightly in), legs firm, pelvis hinges forward. Hands land under the shoulders first with a long concave spine; then elbows bend and the crown may meet floor or a block while weight stays in the legs, not the head.
geometry.svg_hint: Front view: wide stance rectangle base; side view: inverted-V legs + forward-hinged torso; mark crown optional support.

reaction.name: Gross to Void
reaction.summary: School metaphor: attention rides the coarse layer of stance and breath, then thins through half-felt vibration and a single point into quiet. Not a medical or chemical claim.

breath.lands_in: the still gap after the exhale, at the soft crown line
breath.cue: Inhale lengthen the spine long; exhale hinge and settle without dumping weight on the head. Rest one beat in the quiet after sound fades.

orientation.cue: Hinge at the hip creases; keep the spine long; let the crown aim toward the floor only after the back has stayed long.
orientation.gravity: Load the four corners of both feet; legs carry the body. Head is light or supported—never a dump.
orientation.gaze: First stage: look forward with a concave back. Full fold: soft gaze toward the floor or eyes softly closed.
orientation.degrees_hint: Stance roughly 90° between legs (about 4–5 feet for many bodies); elbows near 90° when crown lowers.

attention.primary: The quiet after the last audible edge of the breath or inner sound cue (bindu → śūnya)
attention.secondary: Even press through both feet and lifted inner arches

adiyogi.verse_paraphrase: On any compact (piṇḍa) mantra, move attention along the gross letters, then through half-moon, point, end of resonance, into void—this is supreme meditation.
adiyogi.method_summary: Contemplative class form: take a short inner sound or the breath itself as the ‘mantra,’ notice it thicken then thin—vibration, single point, fade—and rest in the quiet that follows. Do not force occult letter-stages or unpronounceable consonant masses; the teaching is progressive dissolution into silence.

honesty.disclosure: This asana↔method link is a School of 112 Doorways teaching device, not ancient canon. Wide-legged fold and dharana 015 are paired by school index, not by classical one-to-one lineage.
honesty.notes: Edition note: school index = dharana 015 as labeled at hatha.es (piṇḍamantra → ardhendu-bindu-nādānta-śūnya). Many printed editions place related Sanskrit near verse ~42 (e.g. Jaideva Singh / commentary lines); numbering of ‘dharana 15’ vs ‘verse N’ varies by edition. Soft experiential rhyme (gross form thinning toward quiet) is noted but not elevated to inner_logic without stronger textual warrant.

safety.pain_rule: Pain is information. Pause, regress, or exit. Never push through sharp pain.
safety.open_seat_alternate: Keep hands on blocks or a chair with a concave spine; skip crown-to-floor. Soften knees if hamstrings or low back protest.
safety.contraindication_notes: General practice caution only; not medical advice. Use support under hands or head; avoid dumping weight onto the neck. If dizziness appears in the fold, come up slowly with hands on hips.

beats.title: Name the door
beats.script: Door D-015: Wide-Legged Standing Forward Fold — Prasarita Padottanasana. A wide stance that folds the spine long toward quiet.

beats.title: Geometry
beats.script: Step the feet wide and parallel. Firm the legs. Hinge at the hips. Hands under the shoulders first; spine long. Crown may meet floor or a block later—legs still carry you.

beats.title: Orientation
beats.script: Gravity lives in the feet. Keep the head light. Look forward while the back stays concave; only then soften the gaze down as you fold.

beats.title: Breath
beats.script: Inhale four to lengthen. Exhale six to hinge and settle. Six cycles. Land in the still gap after the exhale.

beats.title: Attention
beats.script: Primary lock: the quiet after the last edge of breath or inner sound. Secondary: even press through both feet.

beats.title: Reaction cue
beats.script: School cue only: Gross to Void. Feel coarse stance and sound thin toward a point, then open into quiet. Metaphor, not medicine.

beats.title: Adiyogi thread
beats.script: Safe VBT 015 thread: let a short inner sound or the breath dissolve—vibration, point, fade—and rest in the silence that follows. No forced occult stages.

beats.title: Exit / integrate
beats.script: Inhale, lift the head, hands to hips, rise with a long spine. Feet walk in. Stand quiet for one breath and notice the same quiet without the fold.
